plans.note: No liability/limitation heading appears in the outline; scan the numbered articles following Section 5.4 (general/miscellaneous provisions) for any cap, consequential-damages waiver or 'in no event' language before concluding it is missing.

Development and hosting deals normally carry an IP-infringement indemnity from the host; nothing in the visible outline covers it. Check the back-end general provisions; if absent, raise as missing since HDI builds and hosts the site.

Presence rule — only flag if HDI restricts the Company from operating competing sites or sourcing Deerskin Products elsewhere. Article 1 (site scope/access) is the most likely place for such a covenant.

Watch for language making HDI the sole developer/host or the exclusive channel for Deerskin Products; the site-scope provisions around Section 1.4 are the likely home. Nothing exclusive is visible in the outline.
Direction rule — no pricing/fees section surfaces in the outline. Only flag if the Company is obliged to give HDI terms no worse than those given others; MFN running to us is acceptable.

Section 5.4 appoints project managers/personnel, which is where a hiring restriction would sit if one exists; otherwise likely absent. Only a mutual, time-limited, advertising-carved-out non-solicit is acceptable.

'Termination Date' is a defined term, so a term/termination article exists outside the visible headings. Confirm the Company can exit on notice without penalty and that HDI cannot terminate at will mid-term.
Check the same term/termination article tied to 'Termination Date' for auto-renewal, the non-renewal notice window and any renewal price uplift.
Governing law/venue will sit in the miscellaneous provisions immediately before the signature block at sec-p0072; New York or Delaware is expected for these Hanover Direct entities.

Look in the miscellaneous provisions preceding signatures for assignment/successors language; confirm we may assign to affiliates and successors and that HDI has no change-of-control termination right over us.

Section 1.4 governs HDI's grant of access to the site and related materials; pair it with any ownership/licence article to confirm the Company owns the site content, Deerskin Products data and customer data it supplies.
Section 1.4's access grant is the operative licence; check scope (affiliates and contractors) and that it is not revocable at HDI's discretion.

No audit or records-inspection heading is visible; audit rights running against the Company would most likely appear near any fees/reporting provisions. Only flag if HDI may inspect our books or usage.
Direction rule — search the fee and termination provisions for penalties, early-termination fees or stipulated damages payable by the Company; service credits in our favour are fine and not flagged.

Development/hosting performance standards and any service-level or warranty language should sit in the Article 5 performance provisions around Section 5.4; confirm a meaningful duration and a repair/re-perform remedy.
No insurance heading appears. HDI hosts the site and handles customer order data, so if the general provisions contain no insurance covenant, treat as missing.
Presence rule — check the fee/compensation provisions for minimum spend, guaranteed volumes of Deerskin Products or take-or-pay hosting commitments; nothing visible in the outline.

With 'Termination Date' defined, review the termination article for wind-down obligations, return of site content and customer data, and migration assistance; Section 1.4 access rights may need to survive termination.
